title: Units of measure reference pack
description: Engineering quantities and the units they may be expressed in, each with an exact conversion to one canonical unit per quantity (ADR-014). This schema constrains SHAPE; the physical cross-checks that JSON Schema cannot express (canonical exists, canonical factor is 1, no alias collides with a code) live in validate_packs.py.

label.description: Bilingual label. Both languages are required everywhere: a half-translated pack ships a screen that is half English, which is worse than either language alone.

quantity.description: Stable machine key. Also the key used in unit_preferences JSON, so renaming one silently orphans every stored preference.

canonical.description: Code of the unit every value of this quantity is stored in for comparison. Must appear in units[].code - enforced in validate_packs.py.

minimum_canonical.description: Physical floor in canonical units, e.g. -273.15 for temperature. Checked on the CONVERTED value, so -500 F is caught even though -500 is an unremarkable number.

minimum_note.description: Why the floor exists, for whoever next reads the pack and wonders whether it can be relaxed.

code.description: Canonical spelling, stored verbatim in *_unit columns. Case and punctuation are meaningful: " is inches and ' is feet.

factor.description: canonical = value * factor + offset. Must be non-zero; a zero factor would map every value onto the offset.

offset.description: Affine term, non-zero only for temperature. A DIFFERENCE uses the factor alone - see convertDifference().

datum.description: GAUGE and ABSOLUTE pressures are never interconverted: the gap between them is site atmospheric pressure, not a constant. NONE means the distinction does not apply.

aliases.description: Spellings accepted on input and normalised to code. Matching ignores spaces, hyphens and underscores only - never all punctuation.
